The combination of emtricitabine, rilpivirine, and tenofovir alafenamide is indicated as a complete regimen for the treatment of HIV-1 infection in treatment-naïve adults with HIV-1 RNA levels ≤100,000 copies/mL. It is also indicated for certain virologically suppressed patients (HIV-1 RNA <50 copies/mL) who are on a stable antiretroviral therapy (ART) regimen at the start of therapy, to replace their current ART regimen. The recommended dose is one tablet (emtricitabine 200 mg/rilpivirine 25 mg/tenofovir alafenamide 25 mg) taken orally once daily with food. 2. This combination is also indicated for treatment-naïve adolescents aged 12 years or older who weigh at least 35 kg, as well as for certain virologically suppressed patients (HIV-1 RNA <50 copies/mL) on a stable ART regimen at the start of therapy, to replace their current ART regimen. Safety and efficacy have not been established in patients under 12 years of age or weighing less than 35 kg. For those aged 12 years or older and weighing at least 35 kg, the recommended dose is one tablet (emtricitabine 200 mg/rilpivirine 25 mg/tenofovir alafenamide 25 mg) taken orally once daily with food. 3. Carbamazepine decreases rilpivirine levels by inducing hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated, as it may result in a loss of virologic response and potential resistance to rilpivirine or the NNRTI class. 4. Dexamethasone (systemic) decreases rilpivirine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. Rilpivirine should not be co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inducers due to the risk of virologic failure and resistance. 5. Dexlansoprazole increases gastric pH, leading to decreased rilpivirine levels. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Co-administration is contraindicated, as it may cause treatment failure and/or resistance to rilpivirine or the NNRTI class. 6. Efavirenz decreases rilpivirine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated. Rilpivirine should not be used in combination with other NNRTIs. 7. Adagrasib and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. If co-administration is unavoidable, more frequent monitoring is recommended due to the increased risk of torsades de pointes and other serious arrhythmias. 25. Amisulpride and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. ECG monitoring is recommended if co-administered. 26. Anagrelide and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. 27. Artemether and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. 28. Rilpivirine and atidarsagene autotemcel may interfere with each other. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. Antiretroviral medications should not be taken for at least one month before cell mobilization or the expected duration for elimination of the medications. 29. Bedaquiline and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. 30. Rilpivirine and betibeglogene autotemcel may interfere with each other. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. Antiretroviral medications should not be taken for at least one month before mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. 31. Rilpivirine and givinostat both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. If unavoidable, obtain ECGs when initiating, during concomitant use, and as clinically indicated. Withhold treatment if the QTc interval exceeds 500 ms or if there is a change from baseline >60 ms. 42. Hydroxychloroquine sulfate and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. 43. Isoflurane and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. Discontinue antiretrovirals at least one month before mobilization and until all apheresis cycles are completed. Some long-acting antiretrovirals may require a longer discontinuation period for elimination. 46. Macimorelin and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. Macimorelin causes an increase of approximately 11 ms in the corrected QT interval. Allow sufficient washout time of drugs known to prolong the QT interval before administering macimorelin. 47. Ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir and dasabuvir (DSC) increase rilpivirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. Co-administration of Viekira Pak with rilpivirine once daily is not recommended due to the potential for QT interval prolongation with higher rilpivirine concentrations. 48. Rifabutin decreases rilpivirine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administered, increase rilpivirine dose to 50 mg orally once daily. When rifabutin co-administration is stopped, decrease rilpivirine dose to 25 mg once daily. 51. Sevoflurane and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. 52. Siponimod and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. 53. Tetrabenazine and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. 54. Tovorafenib decreases rilpivirine levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. If unavoidable, monitor patients for loss of efficacy unless otherwise recommended in the CYP3A4 substrate prescribing information. 55. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of umeclidinium bromide/vilanterol inhaled by prolonging the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. Exercise extreme caution when vilanterol is co-administered with drugs that prolong the QTc interval, as adrenergic agonist effects on the cardiovascular system may be potentiated. 56. Rilpivirine increases the toxicity of vilanterol/fluticasone furoate inhaled by prolonging the QTc interval. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative drugs should be used. Exercise extreme caution when vilanterol is co-administered with drugs that prolong the QTc interval, as adrenergic agonist effects on the cardiovascular system may be potentiated. 57. Albuterol and rilpivirine both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 58. Rilpivirine and alfuzosin both prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor patients closely. 59. Aluminum hydroxide decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Modify therapy and monitor closely. If antacids must be administered, they should be given at least 2 hours before or at least 4 hours after rilpivirine. For the combination product dolutegravir/rilpivirine, antacids should be given at least 4 hours before or at least 6 hours afterwards. 60.
